spine: 1. Slack 把「長命 EC2 實例＋持續用 Chef 收斂設定」的舊模型換掉,因為即使有更安全的 rollout、更好的 orchestration、更強的 guardrail,這個模型還是撞到極限——服務層部署難、drift 難免、跨層改動複雜。
2. Shipyard 的核心轉向:把基礎設施當成可部署的 artifact,而不是可以一直被改的 instance;重心從「設定管理」移到「build pipeline、可部署 artifact、自動化安全機制」。

3. 一切從 slack-zero 黃金基底映像開始:AWS Image Builder(取代 Packer)產生、SSM parameter 發佈最新 AMI、EventBridge+Lambda 觸發下游 service pipeline 重建,內建測試在發佈前跑驗證;service team 在上面疊自己的 AMI,base/service 責任邊界由 shared responsibility 模型界定。
4. bake 與 provision 分工把「秒級開機」變成可能:bake 階段把套件安裝等重工作做完並鎖進 AMI,provision 階段只做環境相關的輕量設定(secrets、region、deployment metadata)。
5. Peekaboo(EventBridge+OpenSearch+Lambda)取代 Chef Server 成為 fleet 的 source of truth,連非 Shipyard 部署的 instance 都能追蹤,並提供 UI/API/CLI 三種入口。

6. Gondola 把 AMI 與綁定 git commit 的 Chef artifact 打包成單一可部署單位,透過 executor(ASG Instance Refresh 或 Karpenter)落地;Reaper 用兩種訊號(tainted 事件、超齡)決定何時替換 instance,並用 rate limit 與「大紅按鈕」(S3 全域暫停)控制風險,同時靠 Consul Template 讓 secrets 可以不重建整個 fleet 就更新——這是「semi-immutable」的例外。

7. Ship Quick 讓開發者在 cookbook repo 跑 CLI 測試,Longshoremen worker(分成 vanilla Ubuntu fleet 與 slack-zero fleet 兩組)跑 Chef workflow 並串流 log;整套系統目前撐起數以萬計的 EC2 instance,支援多架構(Graviton ARM + AMD64)與多作業系統,文章未揭露延遲/失敗率/成本的具體數字。

perspective.mechanism: Shipyard 把「基礎設施」本身變成像應用程式一樣的可部署 artifact——用黃金基底 slack-zero + service AMI 分層,配合 bake/provision 兩階段拆分把重工作挪到開機之前,再用 Gondola 統一打包 AMI 與 Chef artifact、Reaper 用訊號與壽命檢查持續汰換有問題的 instance,整條 pipeline 讓「不可變」從一次性部署動作變成持續運作的系統性質。
perspective.tradeoff: 換掉「可以一直改的 instance」,代價是每個環節都要多一層自動化去接手——base 更新後 service team 得主動重建 AMI、要有 Peekaboo 這種獨立盤點系統取代 Chef Server 的 source of truth 角色、Reaper 要靠 rate limit 跟全域暫停鈕去控制汰換節奏;文章本身也承認沒有給出延遲、失敗率或成本的具體數字,只給了「tens of thousands」instance 跟「秒級開機」這種質化的量詞。
perspective.reader_use: 評估要不要把自己團隊的長命 EC2 fleet 換成不可變模型時,可以參考 Shipyard 這種「黃金基底 + 分層 AMI + bake/provision 拆分 + 持續汰換」的組合拳,尤其是 Reaper 的 rate limit 與全域暫停機制,這是避免「不可變」翻車成「同時砍光整個 fleet」的關鍵安全閥。

notes.quote: Even with safer rollouts, better orchestration, and stronger guardrails, the old model—continuously updating long-lived EC2 instances—was hitting its limits.
notes.interpretation: 作者明確主張舊模型(持續更新長命 EC2 instance)已經撞到極限,即使既有的安全措施都到位。

notes.quote: Shipyard is Slack's next-generation EC2 platform. It treats infrastructure as deployable artifacts rather than endlessly mutable instances.
notes.interpretation: Shipyard 的核心定義:把基礎設施當成可部署 artifact,而非可無限被改動的 instance。

notes.quote: Rather than focusing on configuration management as the center of the system, Shipyard shifts responsibility toward build pipelines, deployable artifacts, and automated safety mechanisms.
notes.interpretation: 架構重心從設定管理轉移到 build pipeline、可部署 artifact、自動化安全機制三者。

notes.quote: At the foundation of the Shipyard is a shared base image called 'slack-zero.' This is the core machine image built by Slack's Compute Platform Team and maintained collaboratively with our security and monitoring teams.
notes.interpretation: slack-zero 是整個系統地基,由 Compute Platform Team 建置、跟 security/monitoring 團隊共同維護。

notes.quote: Operating system baseline and hardening, Networking and service discovery configuration, Monitoring and security agents, Common tooling and foundational system configuration
notes.interpretation: slack-zero 內容清單:OS baseline/hardening、network/service discovery 設定、監控與安全 agent、共用工具與基礎系統設定。

notes.quote: To build slack-zero, we use AWS Image Builder rather than Packer. Image Builder provides several built-in advantages over our previous approach with Packer, including: Lifecycle Management: Old AMIs are automatically cleaned up using lifecycle policies, helping reduce storage costs.
notes.interpretation: 改用 AWS Image Builder 取代 Packer,其中一個優勢是 lifecycle management 自動清理舊 AMI、降低儲存成本。

notes.quote: AWS System Manager (SSM) Parameter Publishing: Each new slack-zero image updates an SSM parameter that indicates the latest available AMI for an account. Service pipelines read this parameter to ensure they always build on the most up-to-date base.
notes.interpretation: slack-zero 更新時同步更新 SSM parameter,service pipeline 讀取該 parameter 確保建置於最新基底。

notes.quote: Event-Driven Automation: When a slack-zero image finishes baking successfully, EventBridge and Lambda automatically trigger downstream pipelines in service owner accounts so dependent images can be rebuilt.
notes.interpretation: slack-zero 烘焙成功後,EventBridge 加 Lambda 自動觸發下游 service owner 帳號裡的 pipeline 重建依賴映像。

notes.quote: Built-in Testing: Before an AMI is published, Image Builder launches temporary instances and runs validation tests.
notes.interpretation: AMI 發佈前,Image Builder 起臨時 instance 跑驗證測試。

notes.quote: Each service team builds its own AMIs using slack-zero as the foundation. This allows teams to control their runtime environment while inheriting standardized platform components maintained by the platform organization.
notes.interpretation: 每個服務團隊以 slack-zero 為基礎建置自己的 AMI,自行控制執行環境同時繼承標準化平台元件。

notes.quote: During the bake phase, we install packages and include configuration that is consistent across environments.
notes.interpretation: bake 階段安裝套件、寫入跨環境一致的設定。

notes.quote: Environment-specific settings—such as secrets, regional configuration, or deployment metadata—are applied during the provisioning phase when the instance boots.
notes.interpretation: 環境相關設定(secrets、region、deployment metadata)在 provisioning 階段、instance 開機時才套用。

notes.quote: By moving heavy operations like package installation into the bake phase, instances can become operational in seconds rather than minutes.
notes.interpretation: 把套件安裝等重工作移進 bake 階段後,instance 可以在幾秒內(而非幾分鐘)進入可服務狀態;未提供精確秒數。

notes.quote: Peekaboo taps directly into cloud events and instance metadata, providing better telemetry across environments. It can even track instances from non-Shipyard deployments, giving us a complete view of the entire fleet in one place.
notes.interpretation: Peekaboo 直接接雲端事件與 instance metadata,連非 Shipyard 部署的 instance 都能追蹤,提供整個 fleet 的完整視圖。

notes.quote: We built Peekaboo using AWS EventBridge, OpenSearch, and Lambda.
notes.interpretation: Peekaboo 的技術堆疊:AWS EventBridge、OpenSearch、Lambda。

notes.quote: It has everything teams need: a UI to explore the fleet, an API for integrations, and a command-line interface (CLI) for quick command-line checks.
notes.interpretation: Peekaboo 提供 UI、API、CLI 三種使用入口。

notes.quote: When Gondola builds an artifact, it produces a deployable package for a service with two main parts: The AMI to roll out across the fleet, The Chef artifact containing versioned recipes associated with a Git commit
notes.interpretation: Gondola 的部署包由 AMI 與綁定 git commit 的 Chef artifact 兩部分組成。

notes.quote: Gondola treats these together as a single deployable unit.
notes.interpretation: AMI 與 Chef artifact 被 Gondola 當成單一可部署單位處理。

notes.quote: The executor updates the launch template with the new AMI and configuration. Chef code is packaged to Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3), and new instances use a baked-in bootstrapper to fetch the correct artifact and run the relevant recipes.
notes.interpretation: ASG 路徑:executor 更新 launch template,Chef code 包進 S3,新 instance 用內建 bootstrapper 抓 artifact 跑 recipe。

notes.quote: The executor tells Karpenter which AMI to use and provides the same configuration metadata.
notes.interpretation: Kubernetes worker 路徑:executor 告訴 Karpenter 該用哪個 AMI,附上同一份設定 metadata。

notes.quote: For services with special deployment needs, Gondola makes it easy to add new executors.
notes.interpretation: Gondola 對特殊部署需求的服務,容易擴充新的 executor。

notes.quote: For Auto Scaling Groups (ASGs), we use AWS Instance Refresh, and Kubernetes worker fleets use Karpenter for lifecycle-driven updates.
notes.interpretation: 艦隊層級更新:ASG 用 AWS Instance Refresh,Kubernetes worker fleet 用 Karpenter 做 lifecycle-driven 更新。

notes.quote: The Reaper evaluates two primary inputs. First, it consumes signals from external systems—such as security tooling or AWS EC2 events—that indicate an instance may no longer be in its desired state and should be considered 'tainted.' Second, The Reaper performs periodic checks to identify instances that have been running for longer than their allowed lifespan.
notes.interpretation: Reaper 的兩種輸入:外部系統的 tainted 訊號,以及自身排程檢查的超齡 instance。

notes.quote: When either condition is met, the instance is scheduled for replacement according to its service policies.
notes.interpretation: 任一條件成立,instance 依該服務政策排入替換。

notes.quote: This approach helps reduce configuration drift, limit exposure to vulnerabilities, and reinforce the principle that infrastructure should be updated by redeploying rather than modifying systems in place.
notes.interpretation: 用「helps reduce/limit」而非「eliminate」——效果是部分緩解 drift 與漏洞暴露,並非宣稱徹底消除。

notes.quote: For example, while manual remote access remains available for emergency scenarios, manually accessing a production-class node will generate a signal that marks the instance for eventual replacement, supporting our immutable infrastructure goals.
notes.interpretation: 手動遠端登入 production-class node 這個動作本身會產生訊號,標記該 instance 該被替換。

notes.quote: Built-in rate limiting allows service owners to define how many instances can be replaced at a time, scoped by service, region, or availability zone, preventing sudden capacity impacts.
notes.interpretation: rate limiting 讓服務 owner 定義單次可替換的 instance 數量,可按 service/region/AZ 分別設定,避免容量衝擊。

notes.quote: For emergency situations, we provide a global pause mechanism—the 'big red button.' By placing a control object in S3, teams can temporarily halt all Reaper activity across the fleet.
notes.interpretation: 緊急狀況下,在 S3 放控制物件即可讓整個 fleet 的 Reaper 活動全部暫停(「大紅按鈕」)。

notes.quote: While Shipyard instances are mostly immutable, there is an important exception: secrets. Each instance runs the Consul Template service, which allows us to roll out updated secrets from Vault without cycling the fleet.
notes.interpretation: secrets 是不可變模型的明確例外,每台 instance 跑 Consul Template,可從 Vault 捲出更新的 secrets 而不必重建整個 fleet。

notes.quote: Our infrastructure is semi-immutable: the core system and service layers remain consistent, but critical runtime secrets can be refreshed safely as needed.
notes.interpretation: Shipyard 把自己的基礎設施定義為「semi-immutable」:核心系統與服務層維持一致,關鍵執行期 secrets 可按需安全更新。

notes.quote: Developers run a CLI command from their cookbook repo, where a YAML file defines the test cases. Ship Quick packages the cookbook, uploads it to S3, and sends a workflow message to a queue.
notes.interpretation: Ship Quick 使用流程:開發者在 cookbook repo 跑 CLI,YAML 定義測試案例,Ship Quick 打包 cookbook、上傳 S3、送工作訊息進 queue。

notes.quote: A fleet of worker instances—managed by a lightweight process called Longshoremen—picks up the job, detaches from its Auto Scaling Group, runs the Chef workflow, streams logs back to the CLI, and then terminates (unless the developer chooses to keep it for debugging).
notes.interpretation: Longshoremen 管理的 worker fleet 接手工作、脫離 ASG、跑 Chef workflow、串流 log 回 CLI,完成後終止(除非開發者選擇保留除錯)。

notes.quote: We run Longshoremen in two separate worker fleets because of how our bootstrapping works. The vanilla Ubuntu fleet is used to bake and test the base slack-zero image—it can't build on top of itself, so starting from a clean Ubuntu AMI is required. The slack-zero fleet is for service team cookbooks, which depend on the pre-baked slack-zero AMI.
notes.interpretation: Longshoremen 分兩支獨立 worker fleet:vanilla Ubuntu fleet 烘焙測試 slack-zero 本身,slack-zero fleet 服務依賴 slack-zero 的各團隊 cookbook。

notes.quote: This afforded us far more reliability and operational control across tens of thousands of EC2 instances.
notes.interpretation: Shipyard 讓 Slack 在「tens of thousands」EC2 instance 規模下拿到遠比過去更高的可靠性與操作控制力;數字是模糊量詞,未給精確值。

notes.quote: The platform is designed from the start to support multiple CPU architectures, including both AMD64 and ARM-based Graviton instances, with support for multiple operating systems such as Ubuntu, RHEL, and Amazon Linux.
notes.interpretation: 多架構(AMD64、ARM Graviton)與多作業系統(Ubuntu、RHEL、Amazon Linux)支援;用「designed from the start」帶有一定的未來導向措辭。

notes.quote: Shipyard is particularly valuable for workloads that cannot migrate to containers, such as infrastructure components, Kubernetes worker nodes, and our egress network stacks.
notes.interpretation: Shipyard 對無法搬進容器的工作負載特別有價值:基礎設施元件、Kubernetes worker node、egress network stack。

notes.quote: Shipyard's layered image model is built on a clear shared responsibility between platform teams and service teams. The Compute, Security, and Monitoring teams manage the base layer, making sure it includes all global infrastructure components, security patches, and essential configurations. Service teams then build their own AMIs on top of this base, adding the software and settings specific to their service.
notes.interpretation: shared responsibility 模型:base 層由 Compute/Security/Monitoring 團隊管,service 層由各服務團隊自行建置。

notes.quote: Whenever the Compute team rolls out a fix or update—whether it's a security patch, a monitoring agent update, or a networking change—service teams are responsible for incorporating the updated base into their own AMIs.
notes.interpretation: Compute team 推出更新後,service team 有責任把新版基底併回自己的 AMI。

claims.note: 此為 opener 反直覺畫面的來源依據,逐字對應。

claims.claim_text: 內建的 rate limiting 讓服務 owner 自己定義單次最多能同時換幾台,而且可以按 service、region 或 availability zone 分開設定上限
claims.evidence: Built-in rate limiting allows service owners to define how many instances can be replaced at a time, scoped by service, region, or availability zone, preventing sudden capacity impacts.
claims.note: widget 的 5/36 示範明確標註為示意、非 Slack 實際門檻,無虛構數字問題。

claims.claim_text: 緊急時還有一個「big red button」——在 S3 放一個控制物件,就能讓整個 fleet 的 Reaper 活動全部暫停
claims.evidence: For emergency situations, we provide a global pause mechanism—the 'big red button.' By placing a control object in S3, teams can temporarily halt all Reaper activity across the fleet.

claims.claim_text: 每台 instance 都跑著 Consul Template 服務,可以把 Vault 裡更新過的 secrets 動態捲出去,不必為了換一把金鑰重建整個 fleet
claims.evidence: Each instance runs the Consul Template service, which allows us to roll out updated secrets from Vault without cycling the fleet.

claims.claim_text: 開發者在 cookbook repo 裡跑一個 CLI 指令,YAML 檔案定義好測試案例,Ship Quick 把 cookbook 打包、上傳到 S3,送一則工作訊息進 queue
claims.evidence: Developers run a CLI command from their cookbook repo, where a YAML file defines the test cases. Ship Quick packages the cookbook, uploads it to S3, and sends a workflow message to a queue.

claims.claim_text: 一批 worker instance,由一個叫 Longshoremen 的輕量 process 管理——它把自己從所屬的 Auto Scaling Group 摘掉、跑 Chef workflow、把 log 即時串回 CLI,跑完就終止,除非開發者選擇留著除錯
claims.evidence: A fleet of worker instances—managed by a lightweight process called Longshoremen—picks up the job, detaches from its Auto Scaling Group, runs the Chef workflow, streams logs back to the CLI, and then terminates (unless the developer chooses to keep it for debugging).

claims.claim_text: Longshoremen 分成兩支獨立的 worker fleet...vanilla Ubuntu fleet 專門烘焙跟測試 slack-zero 本身...slack-zero fleet 服務各團隊的 cookbook
claims.evidence: We run Longshoremen in two separate worker fleets because of how our bootstrapping works. The vanilla Ubuntu fleet is used to bake and test the base slack-zero image—it can't build on top of itself, so starting from a clean Ubuntu AMI is required. The slack-zero fleet is for service team cookbooks, which depend on the pre-baked slack-zero AMI.
claims.note: bootstrap 順序因果逐字對應來源。

claims.claim_text: Shipyard 從一開始就設計成同時支援多種 CPU 架構——AMD64 跟 ARM 架構的 Graviton instance 都在內,作業系統也涵蓋 Ubuntu、RHEL、Amazon Linux
claims.evidence: The platform is designed from the start to support multiple CPU architectures, including both AMD64 and ARM-based Graviton instances, with support for multiple operating systems such as Ubuntu, RHEL, and Amazon Linux.
claims.note: note 標為 hedged(「designed from the start」),post 以「從一開始就設計成」對應,未上調強度。

claims.claim_text: 這套模型特別適合那些沒辦法搬進容器的工作負載——基礎設施元件本身、Kubernetes worker node,還有 Slack 自己的 egress network stack
claims.evidence: Shipyard is particularly valuable for workloads that cannot migrate to containers, such as infrastructure components, Kubernetes worker nodes, and our egress network stacks.

claims.claim_text: 合理的推測是,這也是為什麼即使 Slack 已經有更安全的 rollout...舊模型還是撞到了極限——這幾樣工具處理的都是「怎麼更安全地改」,沒有一樣改變「機器持續被改」這個根本形狀
claims.note: 以「合理的推測是」明確標記為作者綜合;來源只陳述舊模型撞到極限(n01),未給此因果解釋。合法標記推斷。

claims.claim_text: 合理的推測是,這也是為什麼 Slack 需要一個跟部署機制脫鉤、自己接雲端事件的獨立盤點系統:只靠部署工具回報,天生就看不到部署工具管不到的那些機器
claims.note: 明確標記推斷;來源只述 Peekaboo 能追蹤非 Shipyard 部署 instance(n14),此「為什麼」是作者推理。

claims.claim_text: 這個對比是兩段原文各自描述的機制合起來看的結果,原文本身沒有直接點名這個差異(ASG 由 instance 主動抓 vs Karpenter 由 Gondola 主動指定)
claims.note: 作者自行標記此對比為兩段原文合看的綜合、原文未直接點名;為合法標記推斷。

claims.claim_text: 合理的推測是,需要兩種 executor 的根本原因,是這兩種艦隊本來就是不同的管理模型——ASG 是一群共用同一份 launch template 的傳統 EC2 instance...Karpenter 管的是跟著 pod 排程動態長出來的 Kubernetes worker node
claims.note: 明確標記推斷;來源只述兩種 executor 存在(n22),未解釋根本原因。

claims.claim_text: 合理的推測是,背後的邏輯是——一台機器一旦被手動改動過,它跟「這版 AMI 應該長什麼樣子」之間的對應關係就不再可信,乾脆換一台重新從映像長出來
claims.note: 明確標記推斷;來源述手動存取產生汰換訊號(n26),此背後邏輯是作者解讀。

claims.claim_text: 合理的推測是,這個例外是「不得不」的妥協——secrets 輪替本身通常是安全維運裡的高頻動作...
claims.note: 明確標記推斷;來源述 secrets 為例外並用 Consul Template(n29/n30),此「為何是妥協」是作者推理。

claims.claim_text: 合理的推測是,先摘掉 ASG 這一步是為了不讓 ASG 自己的健康檢查跟自動擴縮邏輯,誤把一台正在跑測試...的 worker 當成異常實例處理
claims.note: 明確標記推斷;來源述 Longshoremen 會 detach from ASG(n32),未解釋原因。

claims.claim_text: 合理的推測是,這種「先分層、再自動汰換」的模式之所以能撐住數以萬計的 instance,關鍵...在 Peekaboo、Gondola、Reaper 三者各自只做一件事、彼此靠事件跟 metadata 鬆耦合串起來
claims.note: 明確標記推斷;來源給出 tens of thousands 規模(n34),此「為何能撐住」的架構歸因是作者綜合。
